fact: A dim red dwarf in the Great Bear — one of the closest stars to the Sun, yet invisible to the eye.
bio: Lalande 21185 is a red dwarf about 8.3 light-years away in Ursa Major, among the nearest star systems to the Sun. Despite its nearness it is far too faint to see without a telescope, and it drifts across the sky with a large proper motion. Careful measurements point to a family of planets orbiting it.
cultural: It carries no ancient name — only its entry number in the 18th-century star catalogue of the French astronomer Joseph Jérôme de Lalande. Such faint nearby stars became important only once astronomers began measuring stellar distances and motions.
